verdict.rationale: Brex documents an official MCP server that lets AI assistants "manage expenses" and review transactions, plus a Transactions API, so an external agent can pull expense and transaction data. However, the Transactions API is described as view-only. Nothing shows an external agent filtering for uncoded items or writing categories, GL coding or policy flags back for review. The AI categorization and audit features belong to Brex's own built-in agents, not to an API or MCP surface. The only policy data exposed via API is a read-only travel-booking `policy` field. Missing for 10: documented API/MCP query for uncoded transactions, documented write-back endpoints for categories, accounting codes and policy flags, a review-queue handoff for agent-proposed coding, and independent hands-on corroboration.
